title: Rabbi Yosei bar Ketzarta
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: We find in Shabbat 151b that Rabbi Yohanan reported in his name; likewise in Sanhedrin 103b, according to the She’iltot’s reading.

He is also mentioned in Bereshit Rabbah, beginning of chapter 14; Tanchuma, Noach 1 and Metzora 17; and Jerusalem Talmud Shabbat 2:6, with his valuable homily on why the commandments of challah and lighting the lamp were entrusted to women. In Rosh Hashanah 4:8, Rabbi Tachlifa of Caesarea said: Scripture says “as a day of trumpet-blowing” (כיום תרועה), “and you shall make” (ועשיתם); Rabbi Lazar bei Rabbi Yosei bar Ketzarta [said]: regarding all the sacrifices it is written “and you shall offer” (והקרבתם), etc. Hyman suggests that the reading should be “Rabbi Lazar in the name of Rabbi Yosei bar Ketzarta.” In Midrash Tehillim 78:7, Rabbi Shimon bar Chanan reports in his name.

notes.text: Hyman proposes בשם (“in the name of”) in place of the patronymic-like בי. The quoted words כיום תרועה ועשיתם and והקרבתם are retained exactly because the exegetical point concerns their wording.

The consulted Shabbat 151b directly has Rabbi Yochanan reporting Rabbi Yosei ben Ketzarta; the tears saying continues at the start of 152a. Hyman’s supplied bar form is preserved. The exact She’iltot reading and proposed change from בי to בשם in Jerusalem Talmud Rosh Hashanah remain Hyman’s reports, not independently inspected edition findings.
